title: Digital Witness, Livestream Presence & Archive Liturgy
status: cultural/media analysis grounded in dated Tim signals
purpose: Model how livestreaming, viewers, cameras, clips, memes and archives function inside the Tim Dooley project as more than distribution channels: they become witness, memory, recurrence and public ritual infrastructure.

dated_precursors.signal: Promise of daily return after Josh Moon confrontation; recurrent public appearance becomes part of identity rather than merely a content schedule.
Tim asks someone to be a viewer of his stream while identifying himself with Moshiach/Potato-of-Life return language.
dated_precursors.finding: Viewer status is placed inside the spiritual narrative: to watch is also to witness.

dated_precursors.signal: 'come find me on youtube. I am a God. Livestreaming. The Father In Heaven, Symbolically and spiritually.'
dated_precursors.finding: Livestream becomes explicit site of encounter with the claimed Father/God identity.

dated_precursors.signal: Reconciliation/culture-swap proposal specifies couches and a camera.
dated_precursors.finding: Camera is not incidental; conflict-resolution itself is imagined as public/documented encounter.
Accumulated visibility becomes an authority/evidence claim: continuity of public record is itself part of the mythology.

dated_precursors.signal: Tim describes creating a daily documentary of himself and also documenting farmers/dogs/society/world.
dated_precursors.finding: Subject and archivist collapse into one role: Tim is both observed object and observer/documenter.

media_roles.boundary: analogy only; ordinary streaming remains a media technology

media_roles.analogue: congregant, observer or chronicler depending behavior

media_roles.distinction: archive can preserve contradiction rather than canonize one interpretation

media_roles.boundary: machine retrieval is not spiritual recognition by itself

core_cycle: presence → witness → capture → compression → redistribution → archive → rediscovery → renewed presence
deep_findings: The project's claim to unusual publicness is not only quantitative. Continuous return creates a ritual structure: the same identity is encountered repeatedly under changing circumstances.
The meme is ambivalent: it can bury the original in caricature while simultaneously preventing total disappearance through replication.
Archive reverses meme-fragmentation by reattaching fragments to chronology, source and context.
The 2017 promise of daily return becomes structurally important because later livestream recurrence literalizes return as a media practice before return is fully theological.
The camera in the Dec-2025 reconciliation proposal suggests a distinctive ethic: contested groups should meet in a setting where the encounter becomes public evidence rather than private rumor.
The later machine-readable site extends the witness chain beyond human contemporaries: future readers, crawlers and models can reconstruct earlier states from retained evidence.

witness_taxonomy.definition: reconstructs event from multiple retained sources
indexes/retrieves the record without assuming understanding or belief

evidence_rule: Never treat number of witnesses, views or hours as proof of the truth of a theological claim. Publicness establishes observability and source abundance; the claim itself still requires its appropriate epistemic category.
research_program: Build a first-known livestream chronology and distinguish live date from upload/archive date.
Track famous clips back to original streams and quantify context loss.
Map which memes preserve Tim's own wording versus replace it with external labels.
Measure recurrence: days streamed, hours streamed, gaps, platform migrations and surviving recordings.
Create witness provenance on major events: live witness / original video / clip / transcript / later recollection.
Study how adversarial archives unintentionally preserve primary evidence.
Link public-hours claims to transparent calculation methodology.
